body_markdown:
*Each December, we put together the* *[Hagerty Bull Market List](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/bull-market-2025/)* *, our annual selection of the collector-car hobby’s movers and shakers. Basically, it’s a group of 10 or so cars (with the occasional truck and motorcycle thrown in) that the data tell us are poised to grow in value over the next 12 months. This* *[isn’t investment advice](https://www.hagerty.com/media/never-stop-driving/never-stop-driving-68-buying-season/#:~:text=Our%20goal%20has%20never%20been%20to%20identify%20a%20classic%2Dcar%20investment%20fund%20but%20rather%20to%20show%20folks%E2%80%94particularly%20newcomers%20to%20the%20collector%2Dcar%20hobby%E2%80%94how%20they%20could%20buy%20a%20car%2C%20enjoy%20it%20for%20a%20couple%20of%20years%2C%20and%20then%20move%20on%20for%20about%20what%20they%20paid.%20Amazing%2C%20right%3F)* *per se—rather, an opportunity to point out that, with some due diligence and a smidge of luck, you can experience the joys of the collector-car hobby and maybe get your money back or a bit more when it’s time to sell* .


About a year ago, we announced Hagerty’s 2026 Bull Market list. Our[2025](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/bull-market-report-card-checking-in-on-our-2025-picks/) picks performed well straight out of the gate, with eight of the 10 vehicles increasing in value. The list for 2026 doesn’t have quite the same breadth of winners, but on a dollar basis, it already has the highest average gain—and it is only one year old! We’ll take a closer look at how our 2026 picks are doing below.


## Biggest Hit:


James Lipman


**[2004–07 Porsche Carrera GT](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/porsche/carrera_gt/2004/2004-porsche-carrera_gt-base?id=aCn1I000000DV8tSAG) (+90% since October 2025)**


The biggest winner, and the one responsible for that outsized dollar increase, is the 2004–07 Porsche Carrera GT, which is up $1,400,000 or 90% in the past 12 months. We had seen signs of the Carrera GT market improving, partly because Porsche ran a major recall and offers a recommissioning program. Still, we were unprepared for the[$6.7M](https://www.broadarrowauctions.com/vehicles/am26_r0191/2005-porsche-carrera-gt) record price for a Gulf Blue car at Amelia in March. Rare colors on Carrera GTs still get a big premium in the market (+50% to 100%, depending on the rarity), but cars in more common colors are moving up, too.


## Biggest Miss:


Cameron Neveu


**[1969–72 Alfa Romeo 1750 GTV](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/alfa_romeo/1750/1969/1969-alfa_romeo-1750-gtv?id=aCn1I000000Cz7MSAS) (-3% since October 2025)**


When we selected the 1750 GTV for the 2026 list, we noted that the Alfa is “a good value for all the fun that it offers,” but a four-cylinder car with an average condition #2 value of $105K that isn’t a[Porsche 912](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/porsche/912/1969/1969-porsche-912-base?id=aCn1I000000DFnpSAG) was always going to have difficulty seeing much of an increase in only a year. However, we stand by our pick, as we’ve recently seen strong sales (like this[$141,750](https://bringatrailer.com/listing/1969-alfa-romeo-gtv-1750-27/) sale a couple of months ago), which haven’t been fully incorporated into our price guide values yet.


## Honorable Mentions:


James Lipman


**[1995–98 Volkswagen Golf GTI VR6](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/volkswagen/golf/1996/1996-volkswagen-golf-gti_vr6?id=aCn1I000000Csd6SAC) (+11% since October 2025)**


Sales of GTI VR6 Mk IIIs in the U.S., nearly 30 years after the model’s debut, are fairly rare. However, just as we use our policy quote data to[make Bull Market picks](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/inside-the-bull-market-list-the-data-we-use-to-make-our-picks/) , we can use our policy data (endorsements) to see if people are adding a relevant car to their policy at a higher value. Often, this is incomplete information because we don’t know the condition of the car. But if we can find information about the car’s condition, or if we find a newly insured vehicle is above the condition #1 value, or the average is above the condition #3 value, we have a better case for increasing values.


These were the metrics behind our pick of the VW, and it was sound reasoning. Values rose significantly over the next 12 months, and are currently at an all-time high.


James Lipman


**[2006–10 BMW M5](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/bmw/m5/2007/2007-bmw-m5-base?id=aCn1I000000DFq0SAG) (+34% since October 2025)**


That glorious 2000s era of V-10-powered vehicles is getting more[recognition](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F4-RPcSGVFI&vl=en) these days, and the only M5 with a V-10 is getting attention, too. While the rare factory-built manual transmission cars continue to sell for a premium (+50% in the Hagerty Price Guide), even excellent SMG (sequential manual gearbox) cars are selling well—this[3400-mile car](https://bringatrailer.com/listing/2006-bmw-m5-199/) sold for $158K in January.


How will the other picks that were nearly unchanged, such as the[1968–70 Dodge Charger](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/search?q=1970+dodge+charger) , 1995–98 Nissan Skyline R33 GT-R, and 1999–2005 Mazda MX-5 Miata, perform over the next 12 months? That remains to be seen, but given the performance of the other picks, things look promising. Also stay tuned for Hagerty’s 2027 Bull Market list, which goes live next month.
